 Editors' picks | Epidemics | Mass death Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak passes 10 000 confirmed cases in DRC
 By Rishav Kothari 
 Tuesday, October 27, 2026 18:15 UTC Tuesday, October 27, 2026 18:16 UTC The Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) reached 10 060 confirmed cases and 4 887 confirmed deaths as of October 25, 2026, according to the country’s public health institute. Its situation report, published on October 26, recorded cases across 66 health zones in eight provinces. 
 Image credit: ECDC
 Health authorities in the Democratic Republic of the Congo recorded 10 060 confirmed Bundibugyo Ebola cases and 4 887 confirmed deaths through October 25, 2026. A government report, published on October 26, also showed contact monitoring below the response target, with data available from five provinces.
 The report recorded 96 newly notified cases and 46 deaths as of October 25, including 40 community deaths and six in treatment centers. It listed 2 684 recoveries and a cumulative case-fatality ratio of 48.6%.
 Ituri remained the epicenter, with 7 211 cases and 3 370 deaths. Nord Kivu had 2 309 cases and 1 293 deaths, Haut-Uélé 436 cases and 190 deaths, and Tshopo 83 cases and 27 deaths. The other affected provinces were Bas-Uélé, Sud Kivu, Sud-Ubangi and Nord-Ubangi.
 Distribution of cumulative confirmed cases of Bundibugyo virus disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, as of October 20, 2026. Credit: WHO Contact monitoring remained below the 95% response target. Across the five provinces submitting contact-follow-up data for October 25, teams saw 16 205 of 19 853 listed contacts during the preceding 24 hours, a rate of 81.6%. This was not a complete measure for every affected province.
 The government report said that attacks and threats against response teams, including the killing of a nurse, had prevented Bafwasende health zone in Tshopo from submitting data.
 The World Health Organization (WHO) described transmission as sustained and high-level in its October 23 assessment. Its data through October 20 showed that 50 of 66 affected health zones had reported at least one new case during the preceding 21 days; the other 16 had reported no recent cases.
 Number of confirmed Bundibugyo virus disease cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, by date of notification, as of October 20, 2026. Credit: WHO Number of deaths among confirmed Bundibugyo virus disease cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo by date of notification, as of October 20, 2026. Credit: WHO In Kenya, WHO reported nine confirmed cases and two deaths as of October 26. All nine belonged to one connected cluster, with no evidence of wider community transmission. Twenty contacts were released from quarantine after completing 21 days without symptoms, while 98 remained in quarantine.
 Nigeria confirmed its imported case in Abuja on October 20. The Nigeria Center for Disease Control and Prevention listed 53 contacts in its October 24 situation report, replacing the earlier count of 44.
 Number of confirmed Bundibugyo virus disease cases in Kenya, by date of notification, as of October 21, 2026. Credit: WHO Swiss authorities said the patient was evacuated from Nigeria to Geneva on October 26 and was in stable condition. Her husband was isolated in Zurich as a close contact. He was not reported as a second confirmed case. Investigations into the patient’s source of infection continued.
 WHO’s October 23 update listed cases in five countries since the outbreak was declared on May 15: the DRC, Uganda, France, Kenya and Nigeria.
 Map of parts of DRC affected by Ebola Bundibugyo Virus outbreak in 2026. Credit: ECDC No approved vaccine or specific treatment is available for Bundibugyo virus disease. On October 23, researchers in Bunia vaccinated the first participant in the TUMAINI Phase 2/3 trial, which evaluates candidate vaccines including Ervebo. Ervebo is licensed against a different Ebola virus; its use in the trial does not establish protection against Bundibugyo.
 WHO’s October 23 report still cited its August 14 risk assessment: very high in the DRC, high in countries sharing its land borders, and low for the rest of the African Region and globally. WHO said that assessment was being revised and continued to advise against general travel or trade restrictions.
 Bundibugyo virus spreads through direct contact with infected blood or other bodily fluids, or contaminated materials. Symptoms can appear two to 21 days after infection, and people do not transmit the disease before symptoms begin. Early supportive care can improve survival.
 WHO classifies the epidemic as the largest Ebola disease outbreak ever recorded in the DRC, irrespective of virus species.
 References:
 1 Situation Report No. 164 — DRC’s 17th Ebola epidemic – INSP – October 26, 2026
 2 Ebola disease outbreak caused by Bundibugyo virus — Multi-country – ECDC – October 27, 2026
 3 Twenty contacts of Kenya’s first Ebola case released from quarantine – WHO African Region – October 26, 2026
